clue.text: Mean, and prepared for punch-up?

definitions.meaning: read literally: with hands clenched hard, ready for a fight

explanation.definitionFit: A miser is called stingy in this idiom, and the literal sense is hands clenched as fists ready to brawl.

clue.text: Spinner getting over bouncer, though lacking balance

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above, or over, the second

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
a heavy is a burly doorman or minder, the slang sense of bouncer at a club

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler sends down a bouncer and loses his footing.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a spinner and a bouncer misleads: the spinner is a toy and the bouncer is a nightclub doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with too much weight above is unstable, the literal idiom for being unbalanced.

clue.text: How spice might be approached with caution?

definitions.meaning: playfully read as in the manner of the root spice, a whimsical adverb from that spice's name

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means warily or delicately, an everyday synonym for acting carefully.

clue.text: Half turn cheek to see flower

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters, taken here from the word turn

parts.note: lip is impudence or back-talk, as in 'don't give me any lip'

explanation.surface: Someone turns half their face to admire a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a spring bulb flower, so a specific example of the general term.

clue.text: Annoy with smoke

definitions.meaning: verb sense, stressed on the second syllable: to anger
noun sense, stressed on the first syllable: perfumed fumes from burning resin

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to enrage, and the noun is the fragrant smoke of burnt sticks used in worship.

clue.text: 3 rebuilt an Asian capital city

indicators.note: something rebuilt is reconstructed in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the number written out as a word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cross-reference says an Asian capital was reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' looks like a cross-reference to clue 3, but it is just the number spelt out; 'rebuilt' rearranges THREE into TEHER.
explanation.definitionFit: This older spelling names the capital city of Iran, which lies in Asia.

clue.text: Cunning swine passing through borders of Deutschland, getting round target

indicators.note: the pieces go between, so pass through, the two outer letters
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: art means craftiness or guile
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A crafty pig crosses the German frontier and circles a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The board used in darts is a circular target, so the description fits it exactly.

clue.text: Bag — it has caught

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bag that has been caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention dating from 1920s slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a pouch or bag-like cavity in an animal or plant, a biological synonym.

clue.text: Cold food appears when roast served, they say

indicators.note: signals that the word must be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: the traditional British Sunday roast dinner is eaten on the first day of the week

explanation.surface: Something chilled turns up at the weekend roast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the 'Sunday roast' is the traditional weekly family meat dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-cream dessert with syrup and toppings is served chilled, an example of cold food.

clue.text: Constant force proves quick

parts.note: C is the standard symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to lever is to force or prise something open

explanation.surface: Constant force is shown to be fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick as in quick-witted means intelligent and sharp-minded.

clue.text: Team -might one be beaten?

definitions.meaning: a group of experts or judges
a car body section that is hammered back into shape in a body repair shop

explanation.definitionFit: A group of judges or experts is so called, and a piece of a car's bodywork gets hammered out by a repairer.

clue.text: Sticking with the ability to make oneself understood

definitions.meaning: holding together, the physical sense of cohesion

definitions.text: the ability to make oneself understood
definitions.meaning: clarity and logic in speech or argument

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both things that cohere physically and speech that hangs together logically.

clue.text: I say, cricketer produces surprise

indicators.note: signals the letter said out loud, giving the organ of sight

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
an opener is a batsman who opens the innings

explanation.surface: A cricketer shocks someone with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like an old-fashioned exclamation; instead 'I' spoken is the sound of the organ of sight. An opener in cricket is one of the first two batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that startles or enlightens someone is called this, an idiom for a surprise.

clue.text: Couple needing support

definitions.meaning: a pair, especially of game birds
a strut or prop that holds something up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a pair of shot birds, and also a prop or reinforcing bar.

clue.text: Force rodent to conceal name

indicators.note: the rodent hides the name inside itself

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make a rodent hide its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Electromotive force is the technical name for potential difference, measured in volts.

clue.text: Errant father grabbing mother, then time for tragic consequences?

indicators.note: one piece takes hold of the others, holding them inside
errant means straying or wandering, so the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A wayward dad seizes mum, and later comes disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Errant' looks like a description of the dad but signals the rearrangement; 'grabbing' puts mum and the time letter inside the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftermath is the period of consequences following a disaster, so the definition fits.

clue.text: Lack of sympathy for flood victim?

parts.note: no means none, an absence
ah is a sympathetic exclamation

explanation.surface: Nobody felt sorry for someone caught in the deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical ark builder lived through the Great Flood, so he is playfully called its victim.

clue.text: One's inclined to have problems piercing thick skin

indicators.note: the problems go through and sit inside the skin

parts.note: hide is an animal's thick skin
ills are troubles or misfortunes

explanation.surface: Someone is prone to troubles that get through their tough exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's inclined' reads as 'someone tends to', but means 'one that slopes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope of a hill is literally inclined ground, so the clue describes it cryptically.

clue.text: Encourage with new energy to find cooking ingredient

parts.note: to egg on is to urge or encourage

indicators.note: new letters are made from the old ones, so a rearrangement follows

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone urges another on with fresh vigour to find something for the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The albumen of an egg is used in baking and meringues, so it is a culinary component.

clue.text: Film highlight?

parts.note: the leading performer is the bright spot of a movie, a celestial word for a celebrity

explanation.definitionFit: A leading actor is the main attraction of a movie, and the word also means a bright celestial point.

clue.text: Animal managed to catch cold, I say!

indicators.note: the first piece takes in, or catches, the others

parts.note: ran means managed or ran a business
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
coo is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone managed to get a chill and exclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' is a dated British exclamation of mild surprise, like 'I say!'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a masked North American mammal, a specific example of an animal.

clue.text: Sweet little child

definitions.meaning: a dessert, the British word for the last course
an affectionate name for a small, plump child

explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a dessert is often called this, and it is a fond nickname for a chubby little one.

clue.text: Ceremony that is coming up, one where town is frozen in time

definitions.text: where town is frozen in time

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ceremony approaches in a place stuck in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town was buried by Vesuvius in AD 79 and preserved as it was, as if time stopped.

clue.text: Mark in Italian flower is wood

indicators.note: the mark is placed inside the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Tiber flows through Rome

explanation.surface: A man named Mark sits in an Italian bloom made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut wood for building is called by this word, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Go without reading, perhaps, in lines of music

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the lines of music

parts.note: a stave is the set of five lines on which music is written
reading is one of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic), so R

explanation.surface: Someone does without reading the musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' are reading, writing and arithmetic, so 'reading, perhaps' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without food is to be deprived of it, the core sense of the word.

clue.text: One side of Milan put underground

definitions.meaning: one of the two big football clubs of the city, rivals of AC

explanation.definitionFit: Internazionale is one of Milan's two football teams, and the verb means to bury.

clue.text: Customary rules requiring order either way, needing N in Scrabble

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed inside the word for scrabble

parts.note: to scrabble is to scratch or claw at something
OM is the Order of Merit; read one way then the other it gives the pair OM and MO

explanation.surface: Rules need a pattern of tiles and an N in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrabble' looks like the board game but is the verb to scratch. OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: This body of law rests on custom and judicial precedent rather than statute.

clue.text: Zero go for modern style

parts.note: O looks like zero
to part is to go away or depart

explanation.surface: Zero is the choice for a contemporary fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s abstract style using optical illusions, a modern art movement.

clue.text: Girl appearing in nude for song

indicators.note: the girl is placed inside the word for nude

parts.note: bare means naked
Carol is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl turns up unclothed to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian gondolier's song is called this, a specific type of song.

clue.text: He hardly hit the front half of bike-he was somewhere else

parts.note: ironic: the boxer Muhammad Ali hit very hard

indicators.note: the first half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A cyclist barely touched the front of a bike, insisting he was elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He hardly hit' is ironic understatement for Muhammad Ali, a famously hard-hitting boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of having been elsewhere when a crime happened, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Regret getting way overseas from Britain

definitions.meaning: the French word for a street, across the Channel

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to be sorry, and across the Channel it is the French word for a street.

clue.text: Given more than a taste of Afghan gin, the rebels keep going

indicators.text: Given more than a taste of
indicators.note: a good portion of the phrase, more than a sip, is served up from inside these words

explanation.surface: Rebels sampling Afghan gin are told to persevere.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom urges someone to persevere through difficulty, meaning to carry on.
